newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU, OSCE and NATO confer on Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU, OSCE and NATO confer on Albania.

text.p: The European Union said on Friday it was working closely with the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and NATO to hammer out a coordinated, urgent response to the deepening crisis in Albania.

"The Union is coordinating closely with the OSCE and will liaise actively with NATO and other organisations, so that appropriate action can be taken urgently," the EU said in a statement released by the Dutch presidency.
"The European Union expresses grave concern at the breakdown of civil order in Albania," the statement said.

"It calls upon the government, political forces and other groups throughout the country to refrain from violence and to work for the restoration of order and a return to a proper democratic process, which is the only way to overcome the present crisis," it added.

The European Union reiterated its support for OSCE mediator Franz Vranitzky who was meeting Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino on Friday as part of international efforts to halt more than a month of political violence.
Albania's beleaguered government called for foreign military aid on Thursday to halt spreading disorder as the United States and European nations evacuated nationals from the country.
"The Union expects that the safety of foreign nationals will be safeguarded at all times," the EU statement added.

In Brussels, the Western European Union -- the EU's fledgling defence wing -- said in a statement it was watching events in the Balkan country with "deep concern" and monitoring the situation closely.
It added the WEU fully supported iniatives taken by the OSCE and the EU and issued another appeal for an end to the violence.
"It urgently calls on all the parties not to resort to violence, but to initiate a dialogue so that the democratic process can be resumed," the statement said.
European countries have made it clear they do not want to intervene militarily to restore order.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on a visit to The Hague on Thursday said the Albanian crisis was essentially an internal matter, adding it remained unclear what any western military force would do if sent there.

"It is quite clear that the events there are to a large extent a domestic matter. To put it quite bluntly, if you say we should send troops, then you would have to tell the soldiers what they would do there," Kohl said.
"And if I put this question to you, which I can't answer, then you can see my response."
Kohl was speaking after talks with Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, whose country holds the European Union presidency during the first half of 1997.
